codes.description: Applied when a consumer contacts the furnisher directly, or a bureau relays a consumer dispute, questioning the accuracy of specific account information (e.g. balance, payment history, status).

codes.meaning: Account information disputed by consumer, reinvestigation completed, consumer disagrees
codes.description: Follow-on compliance condition once a reinvestigation has closed but the consumer has renewed or maintained the dispute.
Reflects that the account was closed because the consumer asked for it to be closed, distinct from a lender-initiated closure.

codes.meaning: Identity theft / fraud dispute (FTC Identity Theft Report pathway, FCRA Section 605B)
codes.description: Consumer claims the account or activity resulted from identity theft rather than their own conduct; triggers block/removal obligations distinct from an ordinary accuracy dispute.

codes.meaning: Account not associated with the consumer (mixed file / not-his-not-hers)
codes.description: Consumer asserts the tradeline belongs to someone else entirely, often due to a mixed credit file or lender error rather than fraud.
The same underlying debt or account appears to be reported more than once, inflating balances or account counts.

codes.meaning: Paid or settled account reported inaccurately
codes.description: Consumer states the account was paid in full or settled but the tradeline still reflects an outstanding balance or delinquent status.
Placeholder status while a furnisher's FCRA-mandated reinvestigation of a consumer dispute is still underway; used as a fallback when no more specific code fits.
